'''Damir Filipović''' (born 1970 in Switzerland) is a Swiss mathematician specializing in [[Mathematical finance|quantitative finance]]. He holds the Swissquote Chair in Quantitative Finance and is the director of the [[Swiss Finance Institute]] at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Führender Professor in Finanzrisikomanagement an Swissquote-Lehrstuhl berufen|url=https://resources.swissquote.com/sites/default/files/2019-03/press_release_04062009_2.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190712192310/https://resources.swissquote.com/sites/default/files/2019-03/press_release_04062009_2.pdf |archive-date=12 July 2019 |access-date=|website=Swissquote}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Damir Filipovic|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/csf/|access-date=9 December 2020|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Damir Filipović|url=https://www.sfi.ch/en/people/damir-filipovic|access-date=7 April 2021|website=www.sfi.ch|language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Filipović studied mathematics at [[ETH Zurich]] and earned his Master's degree in 1995. He joined [[Freddy Delbaen]] as PhD student and graduated in 2000 with thesis on mathematical finance titled "Consistency problems for HJM interest rate models".<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Consistency problems for HJM interest rate models|url=https://www.research-collection.ethz.ch/handle/20.500.11850/144529|publisher=ETH Zurich|date=2000|degree=Doctoral Thesis|doi=10.3929/ethz-a-003882242|language=en|first=Damir|last=Filipović|hdl=20.500.11850/144529 }}</ref>

As a postdoctoral [[research fellow]] he joined [[TU Wien|Vienna University of Technology]] (2000), [[Stanford University]] (2001) and [[Princeton University]] (2001) to work on consistency problems for [[Heath–Jarrow–Morton framework|Heath-Jarrow-Morton]] interest rate models<ref>{{Cite book|last=Filipović|first=Damir|date=2001|title=Consistency Problems for Heath-Jarrow-Morton Interest Rate Models|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/b76888|series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics|volume=1760 |language=en-gb|doi=10.1007/b76888|isbn=978-3-540-41493-3 |issn=0075-8434}}</ref> and affine processes and applications in finance.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Duffie|first1=D.|last2=Filipović|first2=D.|last3=Schachermayer|first3=W.|date=1 August 2003|title=Affine processes and applications in finance|url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-applied-probability/volume-13/issue-3/Affine-processes-and-applications-in-finance/10.1214/aoap/1060202833.full|journal=The Annals of Applied Probability|volume=13|issue=3|doi=10.1214/aoap/1060202833|s2cid=6340845 |issn=1050-5164|doi-access=free}}</ref>

From 2002 to 2003, he was an [[assistant professor]] at [[Princeton University]]'s Department of [[Operations research|Operations Research]] and Financial Engineering. As scientific consultant for solvency testing and [[Risk management|risk analysis]] in insurance ([[Swiss Solvency Test]]) he joined the Swiss Federal Office of Private Insurance (BPV) in 2003. In 2004, he became full professor on the Chair of Financial and Insurance Mathematics at [[LMU Munich]]. In 2007, he was appointed as director of the Vienna Institute of Finance and full professor at the [[University of Vienna]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mathematik und ... – Programme – WWTF – Wiener Wissenschafts-, Forschungs- und Technologiefonds|url=https://www.wwtf.at/programmes/mathematics/MA06-002/|access-date=6 April 2021|website=www.wwtf.at}}</ref>

Since 2010, he has been the Swissquote Chair in Quantitative Finance and director of the [[Swiss Finance Institute]] at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

== Research ==
Filipović's research focuses on quantitative finance by drawing in an interdisciplinary manner on fields such as [[Mathematical finance|quantitative finance]], [[Risk management|quantitative risk management]], and [[machine learning]] in finance. It aims at both the advancement of theoretical understanding of [[financial engineering]], and its implementation in the [[Financial services|financial industry]] and governmental policies.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Swissquote Chair in Quantitative Finance|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/csf/swissquote-chair-in-quantitative-finance/|access-date=10 December 2020|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> == Distinctions ==
Filipović is the 2016 recipient of the [[Louis Bachelier Prize]] awarded by the [[London Mathematical Society]], the Natixis Foundation for Quantitative Research and the [[Société de Mathématiques Appliquées et Industrielles]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Louis Bachelier Prize {{!}} London Mathematical Society|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/louisbachelierprize|access-date=9 December 2020|website=www.lms.ac.uk}}</ref>

He is a member and former president (2016–2017) of the Bachelier finance society.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Office|first=Bachelier|title=Former members of the Executive Committee|url=https://www.bachelierfinance.org/former-members-of-the-executive-committee|access-date=6 April 2021|website=Bachelier Finance Society|language=en-US}}</ref>
